interactions.label: A 55-year-old woman from an iodine-deficient region presents with palpitations,

params.question: A 55-year-old woman from an iodine-deficient region presents with palpitations, weight loss, and an irregularly enlarged multinodular thyroid. Serum TSH is suppressed. Which pathological mechanism best explains her thyrotoxicosis?

answers.text: Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins binding and activating the TSH receptor

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes Graves disease, which produces a diffusely enlarged gland with tall columnar cells and papillary infoldings — not an irregularly multinodular goiter.

answers.text: Repeated hyperplasia–involution cycles producing autonomous hormone-secreting nodules

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Repeated cycles of TSH-driven hyperplasia and iodine-replete involution create clonal nodules. Some gain autonomous function, producing thyroid hormone independent of TSH — toxic multinodular goiter (Plummer disease).

answers.text: Viral-triggered granulomatous inflammation with passive hormone release

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes subacute (De Quervain) thyroiditis, a self-limiting post-viral condition — it does not produce a chronic multinodular gland.

answers.text: Sudden iodine supplementation directly stimulating hormone synthesis in a normal gland

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Jod-Basedow phenomenon involves iodine supplementation, but it precipitates thyrotoxicosis in glands that already harbour autonomous nodules — not in a normal gland.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the pathogenesis of multinodular goiter: repeated TSH-driven hyperplasia and involution produce uneven clonal expansion. Some nodules become autonomous, secreting hormone without TSH stimulation — this is Plummer disease.
Toxic multinodular goiter (Plummer disease) arises when autonomous clonal nodules, formed by repeated hyperplasia–involution cycles, produce thyroid hormone independently of TSH.

interactions.label: In subacute (De Quervain) thyroiditis, radioactive iodine uptake is suppressed b

params.question: In subacute (De Quervain) thyroiditis, radioactive iodine uptake is suppressed because the thyrotoxicosis results from passive leakage of preformed hormone rather than active synthesis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. In thyroiditis, follicular destruction releases preformed hormone into the blood (passive leakage). The gland is not synthesising new hormone, so it does not trap iodine — hence RAIU is suppressed. This distinguishes thyroiditis from Graves disease, where uptake is high.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Damaged follicles release stored T3 and T4 passively. Since the gland is not actively trapping iodine for new synthesis, RAIU is low — the key discriminator from Graves disease, where TSI-driven active synthesis produces high diffuse uptake.

interactions.label: A completely encapsulated thyroid nodule with entirely follicular architecture s

params.question: A completely encapsulated thyroid nodule with entirely follicular architecture shows ground-glass (Orphan Annie eye) nuclei, nuclear grooves, and intranuclear pseudoinclusions on histology. The most likely diagnosis is:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Follicular adenoma is encapsulated with follicular architecture, but it lacks the characteristic papillary nuclear features — optically clear nuclei, grooves, and pseudoinclusions — described here.
Follicular carcinoma is diagnosed by capsular or vascular invasion on histology. It does not exhibit Orphan Annie nuclei or nuclear grooves — these are papillary features.

Correct. Despite the follicular architecture, the nuclear features — optically clear nuclei, grooves, and pseudoinclusions — are diagnostic of papillary thyroid carcinoma. Architecture can mislead; the nucleus never lies.
Medullary carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells and characteristically shows amyloid stroma between tumour nests — it does not exhibit papillary nuclear features.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the principle: architecture can mislead, but the nucleus never lies. Orphan Annie nuclei, nuclear grooves, and pseudoinclusions define papillary thyroid carcinoma regardless of the growth pattern.
The follicular variant of papillary carcinoma retains all three defining nuclear features of PTC despite having entirely follicular architecture. The diagnosis always rests on nuclear morphology.

interactions.label: A thyroid tumour shows nests of polygonal cells within an amyloid-rich stroma. S

params.question: A thyroid tumour shows nests of polygonal cells within an amyloid-rich stroma. Serum calcitonin is markedly elevated. Which investigation is MOST important to initiate at this stage?

answers.text: BRAF V600E mutation analysis of the tumour

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: BRAF V600E is the hallmark mutation of papillary thyroid carcinoma, present in about 60% of cases. It is not relevant to medullary carcinoma, which arises from C cells.

answers.text: Radioactive iodine whole-body scan for metastatic survey

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Medullary carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells, which do not concentrate iodine. Radioiodine scanning is useful for follicular-derived thyroid tumours, not medullary carcinoma.

answers.text: Germline RET proto-oncogene testing of the patient and first-degree relatives

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Twenty-five percent of medullary thyroid carcinomas are hereditary, driven by germline RET mutations (MEN 2A/2B). Identifying a mutation in relatives triggers prophylactic thyroidectomy, ideally before age five.

answers.text: TP53 mutation analysis to assess dedifferentiation risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: TP53 mutations are characteristic of anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, which arises by dedifferentiation of existing differentiated carcinomas — a different pathogenetic pathway.

overallFeedback.feedback: The amyloid stroma and elevated calcitonin identify medullary thyroid carcinoma. Since one-quarter of cases are hereditary (RET mutations, MEN 2A/2B), germline genetic testing of the patient and first-degree relatives is the most important investigation.

Amyloid stroma and elevated calcitonin identify medullary thyroid carcinoma (C-cell origin). Since 25% are hereditary (germline RET mutations), genetic testing is the most critical next step — it can save lives through prophylactic thyroidectomy in mutation carriers.

interactions.label: A patient with end-stage renal disease undergoes a successful renal transplant.

params.question: A patient with end-stage renal disease undergoes a successful renal transplant. Six months later, serum calcium is elevated and intact parathyroid hormone remains persistently high despite normalised renal function. All four parathyroid glands remain enlarged. This condition is best classified as:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Primary hyperparathyroidism typically involves a single parathyroid adenoma with autonomous secretion — not four-gland enlargement developing in the context of chronic renal disease.

Secondary hyperparathyroidism is a compensatory response to chronic hypocalcaemia from CKD. Once renal function is restored, the stimulus is removed — persistent autonomous secretion indicates progression beyond the compensatory phase.

Correct. Prolonged secondary hyperparathyroidism causes all four parathyroid glands to become autonomous through sustained chief cell hyperplasia. They continue secreting PTH even after renal transplantation corrects the original hypocalcaemia.
Malignancy-associated hypercalcaemia is mediated by PTH-related protein (PTHrP), not intact PTH itself, and does not cause four-gland parathyroid enlargement.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the progression: CKD causes chronic hypocalcaemia → all four parathyroid glands undergo compensatory chief cell hyperplasia (secondary HPT). If stimulation is prolonged, the glands become autonomous — persisting even after a transplant restores calcium homeostasis. This is tertiary hyperparathyroidism.

Tertiary hyperparathyroidism occurs when chronically stimulated parathyroid glands become autonomous. They continue secreting PTH independently even after a successful transplant corrects the underlying renal failure.
